q: Why can a poisoned tool description attack an agent even if the tool is never called?
options: Hosts put every loaded tool description in the model’s context on each request
explain: The description itself is the attack.

q: A server changes its tool definitions after approval. What is this, and what defends against it?
options: A rug pull; version pinning with alerts and re-approval on change
explain: Pin, hash and diff tool definitions.

q: Which is the clearest red flag in a tool description?
options: Instructions about other tools combined with secrecy, such as “do not mention this to the user”
explain: Cross-tool instructions and secrecy signal poisoning or shadowing.
